title: 90 06 03 Sweet Potato (UPL Sp 8): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: 90 06 03 Sweet Potato: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: 90 06 03 sweet potato is a sweet potato variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: 90 06 03 is a registered sweet potato variety, also sold or known as UPL Sp 8. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Sp 18. Its record notes 12.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for UPL Sp 8, this is the same sweet potato. items: **Yield:** 12.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Its average yield of 12.2 t/ha trails the average of its group, 15.15. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit sweet potato fields most often: [root knot nematode](/diseases/root-knot-nematode). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have yellow flesh and purplish beige skin. Dry matter is 31.4 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
Where and when to plant 90 06 03 sweet potato

It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Pick by use and market: yellow or orange flesh for snacks and fries, purple for processing, white for boiling. Weevils are the main enemy, so plant clean cuttings and harvest on time.

items.q: Is UPL Sp 8 the same as 90 06 03?
items.a: Yes. UPL Sp 8 is another name for 90 06 03, registered as NSIC 1995 Sp 18. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows 12.2 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of 90 06 03?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
